chunks.content: # CLO Beginner's Guide: Core Tools - Scheduling This document explains the core tools and procedures for arranging clothing patterns onto a 3D model in CLO, covering automatic and manual arrangement methods, arrangement points, parameter adjustments, and panel positioning for various garment parts. ## Core Tools Arrangement and Automatic 3D Arrangement This section covers how to access CLO's core tools for arranging garment patterns and using the Automatic 3D Arrangement feature to position a 2D version of clothing onto a 3D model efficiently. - Open the Library panel in CLO. - Select **Connect** and choose **CLO Training** from the official account. - Search for **Core Tools Automatic Arrangement**, then double-click to open it. - Close the library; the current version of the garment pattern will be displayed in 2D. - To transfer the 2D garment pattern onto the 3D model, use the **Automatic 3D Arrangement** tool. - Click **Run** to initiate automatic positioning based on the garment's shape. - Confirm the arrangement; the pattern will be automatically placed on the model. - This automatic arrangement saves time and provides a base for further adjustments. ## Manual Arrangement and Arrangement Points Overview This section explains manual arrangement of garment panels on the model using arrangement points, which are visual guides on the model to assist precise positioning. - Open the Library again, select the core tool **Arrangements**, and double-click to open. - Confirm to start a new project file and close the library. - Enable the **Virtual Model Information Display** to show arrangement points on the model, which appear as blue dots. - Arrangement points include: - **Pure blue points** on the center axis, representing asymmetric arrangement points. - **Blue points with white circles** on both sides, indicating symmetrical arrangement points. - To manually arrange a panel: - Left-click to select the panel in 2D. - Hover over an arrangement point on the model; a gray preview will appear showing the potential position. - Choose the desired arrangement point and left-click to set it. - This method allows precise control over where each panel is positioned relative to the model. ## Arranging Front, Back, and Belt Panels with View Switching This section details how to arrange garment panels on different views of the model, including front, back, and belt panels, using keyboard shortcuts for efficient navigation. - Use the **arrow keys** to switch between front and back views. - Arrange the back panels similarly to the front, noting symmetrical arrangement means positioning one side automatically reflects on the other. - Use key **8** to switch to the reverse (back) view for belt panel arrangement. - After placement, open the **Attribute Editor** on the right. - Scroll to the bottom to access arrangement parameters for fine adjustments. - Parameters include: - **X-axis**: Rotates the panel around the model's body horizontally. - **Y-axis**: Moves the panel vertically along the model. - **Distance (Y-axis value)**: Controls the distance between the panel and the model's surface. - **Direction**: Changes the orientation of the entire panel.

chunks.content: - Use key **8** to switch to the reverse (back) view for belt panel arrangement. - After placement, open the **Attribute Editor** on the right. - Scroll to the bottom to access arrangement parameters for fine adjustments. - Parameters include: - **X-axis**: Rotates the panel around the model's body horizontally. - **Y-axis**: Moves the panel vertically along the model. - **Distance (Y-axis value)**: Controls the distance between the panel and the model's surface. - **Direction**: Changes the orientation of the entire panel. - Enter numerical values or use sliders to adjust panel position and orientation precisely. - Press **2** to return to the front view. ## Skirt Panel Arrangement and Positioning This section describes arranging skirt panels on the model, including front and back skirts, using positioning balls for fine-tuning placement. - Arrange skirt panels on the model’s front, middle, and bottom parts. - Use the **positioning ball** tools to adjust placement: - Left-click the green arrow to move the skirt slightly downward. - Switch to the back view using key **8**. - Arrange the skirt at the back similarly. - Use the positioning ball’s green arrow to move downward and the blue arrow to pull the skirt panel slightly forward. - These adjustments finalize the skirt's fit and positioning on the model. ## Summary The arrangement process in CLO involves both automatic and manual methods to place 2D garment versions onto a 3D model. Automatic 3D Arrangement provides a quick initial setup, while manual arrangement using arrangement points and parameter adjustments allows precise control. View switching and positioning tools enable detailed placement of all garment parts, including complex areas like belts and skirts. Mastery of these tools ensures accurate and efficient garment fitting on virtual models.
